subject: Post-call: support/SLA comparisons & proposed side-by-side tests
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.inference>
To: Emily Jensen <emily@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference, marissa_cole@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-11-20T14:05:00-08:00
Subject: Post-call recap & suggested next tests — support/SLA questions

Hi Emily,

Thanks again for the time earlier today — good discussion and really helpful context about the latency-sensitive features you plan to ship in Q1. Quick recap + recommended next steps so everyone is aligned: 

Recap (from our notes)
- Primary use case: real-time document augmentation (sub-second UI paths for token-generation on user events).
- Expected peak: ~35 RPS with 2–3k token bursts for multi-turn sessions.
- Primary concerns: consistent p95 latency, predictable unit cost, and incident support/RCAs.

How Redwood differentiates (short list)
- Serving/runtime optimizations: continuous batching + KV-cache preservation to keep cold-starts low for multi-turn flows.
- Deployment flexibility: hosted API for quick rollout, Dedicated pools for predictable capacity and SLA-backed latency targets.
- Operational guarantees: per-route tracing, token-level cost breakdown, and structured RCA artifacts on incidents.

Support & SLA (quick bullet answers — see attached spreadsheet for numbers)
- Dedicated SLA: 99.95% uptime with 1-hour P0/critical response (pager) and 4-hour P1 response.
- RCA cadence: preliminary incident summary within 8 hours, full RCA and mitigation plan within 72 hours (for Dedicated).
- Logs/audit access: we can share time-bound structured traces and request-level logs for the test window via secure shared Drive; longer retention available as an add-on.

Proposed next tests (to validate both performance and operational posture)
1) 48-hour side-by-side run: your harness + our test runner vs. the hyperscaler you referenced. Target metrics: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail token cost, failure modes under burst.
2) Incident simulation: run a controlled partial-failure (worker drain) to observe fail-over latency and test support response playbook (we’ll time our response from your incident ticket and walk through the RCA timeline).
3) Ops handoff: demo of our Console (traces, per-route dashboards, audit logs) and a dry-run of RCA artifact delivery.

Ask from you
- Can you share the current test harness (or a minimal repro) and a preferred 48-hour window?
- Do you want Redwood to coordinate the hyperscaler side-by-side (we can run both in parallel if you provide auth) or do you prefer to run them from your infra?

I attached a short test plan + SLA comparison sheet. I’ll schedule a 30-minute sync next week to lock down test dates — please suggest times that work for you.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.inference
+1 (415) 555-0123

Attachments: Redwood_vs_Hyperscaler_SLA_Comparison.xlsx; side_by_side_test-plan.md
From: Emily Jensen <emily@acmeanalytics.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.inference>
Date: 2026-11-20T15:22:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & suggested next tests — support/SLA questions

Alex,

Appreciate the clear recap. A couple of clarifying Qs before we lock dates:

1) We had a recent outage with HyperscaleCloud where some inference endpoints experienced 30+ minute elevated error rates; their public postmortem tied the issue to a regional autoscaler bug and they offered credits but the RCA took 10 days to publish. For our security/compliance review, we need to know: what is Redwood’s maximum time to publish an RCA for a Sev 1 (production-impacting) event? Is the preliminary summary you mentioned sufficient for auditors, or do they require a formal RCA doc?

2) In terms of log access: can Redwood provide per-request request/response bodies for the test window, or only metadata/traces? We may need to correlate with user IDs during the test.

3) On credits/financials: HyperscaleCloud’s default credit offer was 10% of the monthly bill for the month of the outage (they also provided no SLA exception). Would Redwood consider a similar one-time concession if an incident breached the Dedicated SLA during our acceptance test?

We’re aiming to get legal/compliance comfortable before we engage our platform team to run the harness.

Thanks,
Emily Jensen
Head of Platform Engineering
Acme Analytics
emily@acmeanalytics.com
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.inference>
To: Emily Jensen <emily@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: sergio_alvarez@redwood.inference, marissa_cole@redwood.inference
Date: 2026-11-20T16:05:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Post-call recap & suggested next tests — support/SLA questions

Emily — thanks, good questions. Notes inline below and next steps at the end.

1) RCA timing and formality
- Preliminary summary: we commit to a brief incident summary within 8 hours for P0s that includes impact window, affected routes, and mitigation status — this is typically what auditors want for an immediate check.
- Full RCA: we target a substantive RCA with root cause analysis, timeline, contributing factors, and remediation plan within 72 hours for Dedicated customers. That document is formatted and signed off by our incident review board; if you need a specific template for compliance I’ll route it to our security team.

2) Log access and data handling
- For the test window we can provide request-level metadata and structured traces (request ID, route, latency, token counts, error codes) and, under an NDA/data agreement, time-limited request/response bodies with redaction options. We do not, by default, ship raw PII-containing transcripts — redaction & sampling policies are configurable.

3) Credits / financials for test incidents
- We don’t pre-commit to guaranteed credits up-front for controlled acceptance testing, but for Dedicated customers we have handled one-off concessions on a case-by-case basis when incidents are within our SLA remit.
- If the acceptance test demonstrates an SLA breach attributable to Redwood (Confirmed P0 downtime per the SLA), I propose we offer an operational credit equal to the pro-rata affected usage for the test window (this is what I’ve seen be effective in prior enterprise deals). I’ll need approval for any amount >15% of the test window bill.

Operational details we’ll commit to for the side-by-side run
- Test harness: we’ll run our agent from a Dedicated pool pinned to a single model variant to match your current config.
- Monitoring: live trace access and a shared incident ticket (we’ll timestamp our first-ack).
- Incident drill: we’ll run one planned worker drain (controlled) and treat it as an incident to exercise the playbooks and time-to-RCA.

Next steps
- If you approve, confirm a 48-hour window and whether you want Redwood to operate the hyperscaler leg in parallel (we can; will need temporary credentials).
- I’ll escalate the credits ask to Sergio for approval beyond the 15% threshold and loop in Legal for the time-limited logs/data agreement.

Cc’ing Sergio and Marissa to expedite approvals. I’ve attached an SLA comparison and the test plan for your review.

Best,
Alex Martinez
Enterprise Solutions — Redwood Inference

Attachments: SLA_Roadmap_v2.pdf; side_by_side_test-plan.md
